context: mega project · licence hold points, nuclear-grade quality and heavy components; a decade from first concrete

brief.intro: New to this project type? A nuclear power plant is a power station built under a nuclear licence. A reactor heats water, the steam drives a very large turbine-generator, and everything that touches the reactor sits inside a massive concrete containment designed for earthquakes and accidents. Three things make it unlike any other plant. First, the regulator: construction, fuel loading and start-up each need a licence, and work stops at defined hold points until the regulator has inspected and agreed. Second, quality: every safety-related item — rebar, concrete, welds, cables — is made and installed under a nuclear quality programme with full records, and work without its paperwork is not complete. Third, scale and duration: thousands of systems, heavy components that take years to forge, and a commissioning programme of two years or more before commercial operation.

must_get_right: Put the licence milestones and regulatory hold points in the schedule as constraints — construction licence before first nuclear concrete, operating licence before fuel load.

Heavy components (reactor vessel, steam generators, turbine rotors) take four to six years to make; their order dates are set before the site work starts and their delivery fixes the 'open-top' installation windows.
Quality records are deliverables: an installation without its documentation is not complete. Plan documentation turnover system by system alongside the physical work.
Commissioning is a multi-year programme organised by system, and it needs systems handed over in a specific order — let the commissioning sequence drive construction priorities from early on.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Construction is organised by building and elevation, installation by area, and — from system turnover onwards — by system and commissioning package, with the licence milestones as fixed constraints.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Multi-shift site calendar. Regulatory reviews and inspections are dated activities with their own durations.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Licence → first nuclear concrete → structures rising with embedded items → open-top heavy lifts → primary loop welding → bulk piping, cabling and I&C by area → system completion and turnover in commissioning order → cold functional tests → hot functional tests → operating licence → fuel load → criticality → power ascension. The critical path runs through the nuclear island civil works to the heavy lifts, then through system turnover and the functional tests.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Design is substantially complete before first nuclear concrete; licences are granted on the assumed dates; heavy components are delivered to their windows; the grid connection is ready for back-feed and for full-power export.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: Nuclear quality programme and security regime on site; very dense reinforcement and embedded parts; congestion inside the containment; qualified welders and inspectors are scarce.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: design changes during construction, quality non-conformances requiring rework, late heavy components, bulk-installation productivity, regulatory findings at hold points, and test failures during commissioning. Contingency is held before each licence milestone.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by building / area, then system; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for area installation crews and system completion teams — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
